page: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The server is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processors operating up to 3.6 GHz, delivering 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with symmetric multithreading. It features 512 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The instance provides 50 Gbps baseline networking throughput, lacks bundled local storage, and contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation shows exceptional parallel processing capabilities, led by a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 191273.61 and a PassMark CPU score of 99308.37. Extended instruction and hardware-assisted cryptography tests also position the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Memory throughput is solid, recording 9076.97 GB/sec for cached reads and 252.01 GB/sec for large-block uncached transfers. Redis SET operations reach 129.17 million operations per second, ranking in the top decile. Single-thread benchmarks show moderate execution speed, with Geekbench single-core recording an average score of 1734.0.

The absence of integrated NVMe solid-state storage requires remote Amazon EBS allocation for non-volatile state. This design isolates disk I/O to network channels while focusing host resources strictly on parallel computation and in-memory execution. The massive core density and 50 Gbps network pipe provide reliable scale-up economics without the premium associated with specialized GPU hardware or higher RAM-to-core ratios.

Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is well tailored for memory-resident caching clusters, high-throughput static web serving, Clang software build farms, parallel batch processing, enterprise ERP deployments, and large-scale relational or in-memory databases.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general purpose instance powered by dedicated 64-core AMD EPYC 7R13 processors delivering 128 vCPUs at clock speeds up to 3.6 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 50 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance provides no onboard local storage, relying exclusively on network-attached block storage, and includes no discrete graphics processing units. Synthetic benchmarking reflects top-tier multi-threaded processing and cryptographic acceleration, paired with strong throughput in Redis operations and static web delivery. Single-thread responsiveness remains within average boundaries. The high core count and ample memory allocation yield efficient resource consolidation for large-scale enterprise services, software compilation, data transformations, in-memory caching layers, and multi-tenant application deployments.
